def stats(k,start,end):
    ts=[(t,v) for t,v in vals[k] if start<=t<end]
    vs=[v for t,v in ts]
    import datetime
    # hourly mean by hour-of-day
    from collections import defaultdict
    hod=defaultdict(list)
    for t,v in ts:
        h=int(t[11:13]); hod[h].append(v)
    amplitudes=[sum(x)/len(x) for x in hod.values()]
    return round(min(vs),2),round(max(vs),2),round(max(amplitudes)-min(amplitudes),2)

The data available is only zone air‑temperature sensors plus heating/cooling setpoints for each zone. The Zone_F3_Z01 sensor shows a normal, preserved diurnal swing that has simply shifted up ~2 °C relative to its neighbors — a signature a constant (or slowly drifting) sensor offset and a real local heat‑gain increase share. There is no VAV supply/discharge air temperature, air‑flow, damper position, occupancy, or CO₂ stream in the store, and no redundant/secondary sensor in this zone that could confirm whether the air itself is warmer on average or whether only the sensor reading has moved.

With the streams that are actually present, I cannot distinguish "local load change" from "zone sensor fault".
